newsitem.title: USA: Miami Mayor seeks lowered reserve requirement.
newsitem.headline: Miami Mayor seeks lowered reserve requirement.

text.p: Miami Mayor Joe Carollo said Thursday he had asked a state oversight board to cut its reserve requirement for Miami to 2.5 percent of the city's anticipated deficit, rather than the 20 percent the board had sought.
On Jan 14, the oversight board rejected the budget the city submitted, saying $9.9 million of the $275 million in revenues the city budgeted for were "too iffy" to count on.
The board also asked the city to set aside $13.6 million of unallocated funds, or 20 percent of the anticipated $68 million deficit, in reserves against uncollected funds or emergencies.

Carollo strongly criticized the board and accused it of putting unduly harsh conditions on the city. He said he met privately on Wednesday with Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay, who chairs the oversight board, before the two attended a state budget meeting Wednesday in Tallahassee.
Carollo said he proposed that Miami set aside 2.5 percent of the deficit, or $1.7 million, in reserves for the fiscal year ending Sept 30.
He proposed raising reserves to 5 percent of the deficit, or $3.4 million, over the next five years.
MacKay did not commit to the plan.
The city must present a revised budget to the oversight board by Saturday, and draft a 5-year budget by April 15.
Carollo described Wednesday's meeting with MacKay as friendly.
"Basically we both worked out of good faith. We tried to work out some differences we had," Carollo said.

Gov. Lawton Chiles appointed the oversight board in December to guide Miami to fiscal solvency. The $68 milion deficit for the current fiscal year was discovered after three top officials resigned to face corruption charges.
